channelTitle: Vasilisa outsmarts Baba Yaga - the skull-lanterns burn - Part 2
hook: Last time, Vasilisa survived her first night in the chicken-leg hut - now Baba Yaga gives her the final test, and the skulls on the fence are watching.
storyParts: Night two: wash the whole hut, cook dinner, and weave fine cloth from rotten flax. Vasilisa despaired - but again the little doll worked while she slept, and by dawn the hut gleamed.
Baba Yaga was furious that the girl survived - but a witch's word is law even to herself. She gave Vasilisa a skull-lantern full of fire and let her walk out of the forest alive.
The girl carried the glowing skull home through the dark trees. When her stepmother and stepsisters ran out to grab the fire, the lantern's eyes flared - and burned all three to ash.
Vasilisa buried the skull, moved into town, and became a weaver so fine that the tsar himself sought her cloth - and later, her hand. Kindness and courage did what cruelty never could.
In old Russia they still say Baba Yaga lives in that walking hut. But they also say she only devours the mean-hearted - the kind ones always find the hidden door home.
cta: Which legend should Grandma June tell next - the Green Children of Woolpit or Baba Yaga's sister? Tell me in the comments.
moral: The cruel send others to die in the forest - and forget the forest has a memory.
